$comment: Evidence map for Phase 29. Executable tests prove integration mechanics and safety policies; live provider persistence and exchange remain declared.

areas.area: Connectors and credentials are tenant-scoped and least-privilege
areas.requirement: Connector lifecycle, integration scope, credential expiry/isolation and least-privilege needs are explicit.

evidence.contains: Every exchange is declared and reversible
creates integration instance with tenant scope
least privilege satisfied only for declared needs

areas.area: Inbound mapping, validation, idempotency and dead-letter handling are explicit
areas.requirement: Unknown or invalid payloads are quarantined/dead-lettered, mappings are declared, and duplicate events are not processed twice.

areas.area: Integration retries, rate limits, synchronization and reconciliation preserve truth
areas.requirement: Retry classes are bounded, provider rate limits are respected, field authority is unambiguous, conflicts are policy-resolved, and reconciliation gaps are surfaced.

evidence.contains: retries only transient and rate-limited classes

areas.area: Protocol translation and AI mapping proposals are governed
areas.requirement: Lossy translations are visible, AI mapping changes require approval in production, mock providers support tests, and production certification requires all gates.

evidence.contains: AI mapping proposals require approval in production
AI never silently alters production mappings

areas.area: Webhook and network security checks fail closed
areas.requirement: Webhook signature, freshness, replay, authentication and authorization are required; network TLS, certificate and allowlist checks are enforced.

evidence.contains: webhook delivery secure only with all checks

areas.area: Integration health, logs, traces, metrics, alerts and audit are attributable
areas.requirement: Provider health, sanitized logs, trace spans, metrics, alerts, certificates and audit events remain observable.

areas.area: Integration governance responds to risk, drift and connectivity failure
areas.requirement: High-risk production entry requires the approval chain, schema drift quarantines according to risk, integrations can pause/disconnect, and store-and-forward handles unreliable connectivity.

evidence.contains: high-risk integrations require full approval chain
evaluates schema drift response by risk
pauses and resumes without deleting config

areas.area: External normalization, identifiers and integration events preserve lineage
areas.requirement: Timezone/currency normalization preserves context, external IDs remain traceable, and integration events are typed and attributable.

areas.area: Live external exchange and durable integration state are wired
areas.requirement: Provider credentials, connections, sync jobs, reconciliation records and integration events persist and operate at an authorized live boundary.
